answer: Answers are hollow claims until someone challenges them: acceptance is optimistic, and a challenge opens a bisection game where each side posts a bond that doubles at every step. An honest challenger needs one true objection, so a fake collapses quickly, while a farm defending k copies must fund k escalation ladders at once. Because a loss burns the whole ladder, the k-th fake costs k times a doubling bond, and the loss sends a ripple through every other claim the same operator holds. Each step is signed with a public plume, so who escalated is on the record.
